Evaluation, for the CPA

Before management’s plans, conditions and events raised substantial doubt. The plans are probable of being carried out (a binding bank commitment whose conditions are in management’s hands) and alleviate the doubt.
The draft note (client)
“Management … has concluded that there are none.” Wrong: there were such conditions (GC-01).
Proposed note wording

Conditions and events, considered in the aggregate, raised substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the financial statements are available to be issued: its $3,500,000 line of credit matures March 31, 2027 and could not be repaid from operations. Management’s evaluation and plans: on October 16, 2026 Cinderbrook Bank committed to renew the line to March 31, 2029, and the board suspended dividends until the renewal closes. Management’s plans alleviate the substantial doubt.
Not this wording
“Substantial doubt exists” describes doubt the plans do not alleviate; it would also put a going concern section in the auditor’s report.
The report (AU-C 570, paraphrased)
With the doubt alleviated, no going concern section is required; the auditor considers the disclosure and may add an emphasis-of-matter paragraph. The CPA concludes.
Before dating the report
Confirm the relief with the bank (COV-01), obtain written representations on the plans (REP-01) and bring the review to the report date (DATE-01).
